blocks.name: Plan first
blocks.what: Write down what the app should do before any code is written, so the build has a clear target
blocks.applies: every app

blocks.name: MVP
blocks.what: Build the smallest version that is useful, and add the rest once it works
blocks.applies: every app

blocks.name: Git
blocks.what: Keeps a history of every change, so any mistake can be undone
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: The project is a git repository, with its first commit on the work branch, not on the main branch.

blocks.name: Branches
blocks.what: A separate line of work, so changes can be tried without touching the main version
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: Build work happens on a branch, not directly on the main branch.

blocks.name: venv
blocks.what: Gives a Python project its own set of packages, separate from every other project
blocks.applies: the project uses Python
blocks.check: Packages install into an environment that belongs to this project only, and a fresh install from the requirements file works.

blocks.name: Env vars
blocks.what: Settings that change per machine, such as keys and addresses, live outside the code
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: Settings that differ per machine come from the environment, and the app starts from the example env file once its values are filled in.

blocks.name: Secrets
blocks.what: Keys and passwords are kept out of the code, out of git and out of logs
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: The real env file is ignored by git, the app reads every key and password from the environment, and the example env file holds no real values.

blocks.name: CLAUDE.md
blocks.what: A file of project rules that the AI reads at the start of every session
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: CLAUDE.md exists, names the one check command, links to docs/plan.md, and lists the "Rules every change follows". The check command runs lint, type checks where the language has them, and every test, and it passes.

blocks.name: Agent memory
blocks.what: Notes an AI assistant keeps between sessions, so it remembers facts about you or the project
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Skills
blocks.what: A packaged set of instructions an AI assistant follows to do one job the same way each time
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Modularity
blocks.what: Split the code into small parts that each do one job
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: Each file has one job that can be said in one line, and no file has become a catch-all.

blocks.name: Separation
blocks.what: Separation of concerns: keep the screens, the business rules and the data access in separate places
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: Screen code, business rules and data access live in separate places, and the rules can be tested without the screen.

blocks.name: Frontend & backend
blocks.what: The frontend is what runs on the user's screen; the backend is what runs on the server
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: API
blocks.what: A set of requests one program can send another, with agreed answers
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Webhooks
blocks.what: Another service calls your app when something happens there, such as a completed payment
blocks.applies: another service must tell the app when something happens, such as a payment
blocks.check: A webhook with a missing or wrong signature is refused, and the same webhook delivered twice has the effect of one.

blocks.name: HTTP status codes
blocks.what: The number every web answer carries to say whether the request worked, and if not, why
blocks.applies: the app has an API
blocks.check: Errors return the matching status code (not found, not allowed, bad input), never a success code with an error inside.

blocks.name: Cookies
blocks.what: Small pieces of data a website stores in the browser, often to remember who is logged in
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Middleware
blocks.what: Code that runs on every request before it reaches a feature, such as a login check
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Edge front door
blocks.what: A service in front of your server that filters bad traffic and serves the app close to users
blocks.applies: the app is going live on the internet

blocks.name: Databases
blocks.what: Store the app's data so it survives restarts and can be searched
blocks.applies: the app stores data
blocks.check: Data that must last is stored in a database and is still there after the app restarts.

blocks.name: JSON
blocks.what: A plain-text format for structured data that almost every program can read
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: SQL
blocks.what: The language used to ask a relational database for data and to change it
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Data modeling
blocks.what: Decide what kinds of things the app stores and how they link together
blocks.applies: the app stores data
blocks.check: Each kind of thing is stored once, related things are linked, and no fact is kept in two places that can disagree.

blocks.name: Migrations
blocks.what: Files that record each change to the database's structure, so every copy can be brought up to date
blocks.applies: the app uses a database with tables
blocks.check: Every change to the tables is a migration file in the project, and a fresh database built from the migrations works with the app.

blocks.name: Transactions
blocks.what: Group several changes so they all happen together, or none do
blocks.applies: one action changes several records that must stay in step
blocks.check: When a save with several steps fails partway, none of its steps stay saved. A test forces the failure.

blocks.name: NoSQL
blocks.what: Databases that store documents or key-value pairs instead of tables
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Threat modeling
blocks.what: Ask what could go wrong, who might attack, and what would hurt most, before building
blocks.applies: the app has logins, money or private data

blocks.name: Least privilege
blocks.what: Give every key and account only the access it needs, nothing more
blocks.applies: the app uses keys, database users or service accounts
blocks.check: Each key and database user can do only what the app needs. No admin or root key is used while the app runs.

blocks.name: Secure defaults
blocks.what: When a setting is missing, the app picks the safe choice
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: With a setting missing, the app takes the safe path: debug mode off, new things private, access refused.

blocks.name: Secret rotation
blocks.what: Replace keys on a schedule, and at once if one may have leaked
blocks.applies: the app is live and uses long-lived keys

blocks.name: Authentication
blocks.what: Checking who someone is, usually with a login
blocks.applies: the app has logins
blocks.check: Pages and actions for logged-in users refuse a visitor who is not logged in, including direct requests that skip the screen.

blocks.name: Sessions vs JWT
blocks.what: Two ways to remember a logged-in user: a record on the server, or a signed token the browser holds
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: OAuth 2.1
blocks.what: Let people log in with an account they already have, such as Google, without giving you their password
blocks.applies: users log in with Google or another provider
blocks.check: Login through the provider works end to end, and the app never sees or stores the provider password.

blocks.name: Magic links
blocks.what: Log in by clicking a one-time link sent by email, with no password
blocks.applies: users log in with an email link
blocks.check: A login link works once and expires after a short time. A used or expired link shows a clear message.

blocks.name: Multi-factor auth
blocks.what: Ask for a second proof, such as a code from a phone, on top of the password
blocks.applies: accounts guard money or sensitive data

blocks.name: API keys
blocks.what: Secret codes that let other programs use your app's API
blocks.applies: the app gives keys to its users or to other programs
blocks.check: A new key is shown once and only its hash is stored. A revoked key stops working at once.

blocks.name: Unified principal
blocks.what: One way to represent the caller, whether they came in by login or by API key, so every check treats them the same
blocks.applies: callers arrive in more than one way, such as a login and an API key

blocks.name: CAPTCHA / Turnstile
blocks.what: A check that tells people from bots on public forms
blocks.applies: public forms attract bots

blocks.name: Hashing
blocks.what: Store a one-way fingerprint of a password, never the password itself
blocks.applies: the app stores passwords
blocks.check: Passwords are stored only as salted hashes made by a password-hashing function. No password appears in the database, logs or error messages.

blocks.name: Brute force
blocks.what: Stop attackers from guessing passwords by trying again and again
blocks.applies: users log in with a password
blocks.check: Repeated wrong passwords for one account, or from one source, are slowed down or locked out.

blocks.name: Authorization
blocks.what: Checking what a logged-in user is allowed to do
blocks.applies: the app has logins
blocks.check: Every action checks on the server that this user may do it. Hiding a button does not count as the check.

blocks.name: Owner-only access
blocks.what: Users can see and change only their own things
blocks.applies: users have their own private data
blocks.check: A logged-in user who asks for another user's item by its id is refused, for reading, changing and deleting.

blocks.name: Role-based access
blocks.what: Different kinds of users, such as admins and members, get different permissions
blocks.applies: the app has more than one kind of user, such as admin and member
blocks.check: Each role can do exactly its allowed actions. A test tries each forbidden action as each role.

blocks.name: Input validation
blocks.what: Check every piece of incoming data on the server before using it
blocks.applies: the app accepts input from users or other systems
blocks.check: Every input is checked on the server for type, size and allowed values. Bad input gets a clear error and is never saved.

blocks.name: XSS
blocks.what: Cross-site scripting: stop text a user typed from running as code in someone else's browser
blocks.applies: a web app shows text that users typed
blocks.check: Text containing a script tag, saved by one user, shows as plain text to another user and does not run.

blocks.name: CSRF
blocks.what: Cross-site request forgery: stop another site from acting through a logged-in user's browser
blocks.applies: a web app keeps users logged in with cookies
blocks.check: A request that changes something, sent from another site without the app's token, is refused.

blocks.name: CORS
blocks.what: Cross-origin resource sharing: decide which other sites may call your API from a browser
blocks.applies: a browser frontend calls an API at a different address
blocks.check: The API allows only the app's own frontend addresses, and never every site together with logins.

blocks.name: SSRF
blocks.what: Server-side request forgery: stop users from making your server fetch internal addresses
blocks.applies: the server fetches addresses that users supply
blocks.check: A user-supplied address that points at this machine, a private network or a cloud metadata address is refused.

blocks.name: SQL injection
blocks.what: Stop user input from being run as part of a database query
blocks.applies: the app uses a SQL database
blocks.check: Every query passes user input as parameters. Input containing quotes and SQL words is treated as plain text.

blocks.name: Content Security Policy
blocks.what: A rule the server sends that tells the browser which scripts and sources a page may load
blocks.applies: a web app is going live

blocks.name: Safe user HTML
blocks.what: Clean formatted text from users so only harmless tags remain
blocks.applies: users can post formatted text or HTML
blocks.check: User HTML is cleaned to an allowlist of tags before it is shown. Scripts and event handlers are stripped.

blocks.name: Path & upload safety
blocks.what: Make sure uploaded files and user-given file names cannot reach places they should not
blocks.applies: users upload files, or a file path comes from user input
blocks.check: Uploads are limited by type and size and stored under a generated name, away from the app's source files (in an upload folder inside the project, or a storage service). A file name containing ../ cannot escape the upload folder.

blocks.name: Open redirect
blocks.what: Stop links that bounce users through your site to a stranger's site
blocks.applies: the app redirects to an address taken from a link, such as after login
blocks.check: A redirect target outside the app's own addresses is ignored.

blocks.name: TLS
blocks.what: Encrypt traffic between the browser and the server; it is the padlock in the address bar
blocks.applies: the app is going live on the internet

blocks.name: Encryption at rest
blocks.what: Encrypt stored data so a stolen disk or backup cannot be read
blocks.applies: the app stores highly sensitive data

blocks.name: Secure cookies
blocks.what: Cookie settings that keep the login cookie away from scripts and other sites
blocks.applies: a web app keeps users logged in with cookies
blocks.check: The login cookie is set with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite.

blocks.name: PII minimization
blocks.what: Collect only the personal data a feature actually needs
blocks.applies: the app collects personal data
blocks.check: Every personal field the app collects is used by a feature in the plan. Nothing is collected just in case.

blocks.name: Security headers
blocks.what: Extra instructions the server sends that turn on the browser's built-in protections
blocks.applies: a web app is going live

blocks.name: Trusted client IP
blocks.what: Work out the visitor's real address correctly when the app sits behind a proxy
blocks.applies: the app sits behind a proxy and uses the visitor's address

blocks.name: Signed device ID
blocks.what: A tamper-proof way to recognise a returning visitor who has no account
blocks.applies: the app must recognise visitors who have no account

blocks.name: Honeypot
blocks.what: A hidden trap, such as a field only bots fill in, that catches automated abuse
blocks.applies: the app is live and being probed

blocks.name: Audit trail
blocks.what: A record of who changed what and when, for the actions that matter
blocks.applies: staff change other people's data, or money moves

blocks.name: Dependency scanning
blocks.what: Check the packages the app uses against lists of known security problems
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: The check command scans the project's packages for known security problems, and fails when it finds a serious one.

blocks.name: Secret scanning
blocks.what: Search the code and its history for keys or passwords that were committed by mistake
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: The check command scans the tracked files and the git history for keys and passwords, and fails when it finds one.

blocks.name: Data retention
blocks.what: Decide how long personal data is kept, and delete it when the time is up
blocks.applies: the app keeps personal data over time

blocks.name: Consent management
blocks.what: Ask visitors for permission before tracking them, where the law requires it
blocks.applies: the app tracks visitors where consent is required

blocks.name: Design for failure
blocks.what: Assume outside services will fail, and decide in advance what the app does when they do
blocks.applies: the app depends on outside services

blocks.name: Bulkheads
blocks.what: Keep parts of the system apart so one failing part cannot sink the rest
blocks.applies: one failing part could take down the rest

blocks.name: Redundancy
blocks.what: Run spare copies so one machine failing does not take the app down
blocks.applies: downtime has become costly

blocks.name: Error budgets
blocks.what: Agree how much downtime is acceptable, and slow new features when it is used up
blocks.applies: a team must balance new features against stability

blocks.name: Chaos testing
blocks.what: Break parts of the system on purpose to prove it recovers
blocks.applies: the app runs on several machines

blocks.name: Timeouts
blocks.what: Give every outside call a time limit, so a hanging service cannot freeze the app
blocks.applies: the app calls outside services
blocks.check: Every outside call has a time limit. With a service that hangs, the app gives up and tells the user.

blocks.name: Retry
blocks.what: Try a failed call again after a short wait, a limited number of times
blocks.applies: the app calls outside services
blocks.check: A call that fails briefly is retried a few times with growing waits, then gives up with a clear error. Errors that can never succeed are not retried.

blocks.name: Circuit breaker
blocks.what: Stop calling a service that keeps failing, and try again later
blocks.applies: an outside service fails often under real use

blocks.name: Error handling
blocks.what: Catch failures, show the user a plain message, and log the details
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: A failure shows the user a plain message and is logged with detail. No raw error or stack trace reaches the screen.

blocks.name: Idempotency
blocks.what: Make sure an action sent twice, by a double click or a retry, happens only once
blocks.applies: an action must never happen twice, such as a payment, an order or an email
blocks.check: The same request sent twice, by a double click or a retry, has the effect of one.

blocks.name: Fallback
blocks.what: Have a backup answer or service ready when the main one fails
blocks.applies: a feature should keep working when one part fails

blocks.name: Graceful degradation
blocks.what: Keep the rest of a feature working when one part of it fails
blocks.applies: a feature should keep working when one part fails

blocks.name: Free-first cascade
blocks.what: Try free sources of data first, and pay for a call only when they come up empty
blocks.applies: the app pays per call for data it could often get free

blocks.name: Concurrency gate
blocks.what: Limit how many heavy requests run at the same time
blocks.applies: heavy requests arrive faster than the app can serve them

blocks.name: Single-flight
blocks.what: When many identical requests arrive together, do the work once and share the answer
blocks.applies: many identical requests arrive at once

blocks.name: Per-host pacing
blocks.what: Space out calls to each outside service so you stay under its rate limits
blocks.applies: the app calls rate-limited outside services heavily

blocks.name: Quota ledger
blocks.what: Keep one shared count of a limited key's usage across all workers
blocks.applies: several workers share one limited key

blocks.name: Load shedding
blocks.what: Turn some requests away quickly when overloaded, so the rest still succeed
blocks.applies: traffic can exceed capacity

blocks.name: Degrade under quota
blocks.what: When a paid quota runs out, switch to a cheaper or reduced mode instead of failing
blocks.applies: the app can run out of a paid quota

blocks.name: Rate limiting
blocks.what: Cap how many requests each caller can make in a period of time
blocks.applies: the app is going live with public or costly endpoints

blocks.name: Background jobs
blocks.what: Run slow work outside the user's request, so the screen answers at once
blocks.applies: some work the user does not watch takes longer than a few seconds, such as sending email, importing a file or building a report
blocks.check: Slow work the user does not watch runs outside the request. The user gets an immediate response and can see whether the job finished or failed.

blocks.name: Dead-letter queue
blocks.what: A place where jobs that keep failing are set aside for a person to look at
blocks.applies: background jobs fail under real use

blocks.name: Idempotent ingest
blocks.what: Process each incoming message from another system only once, even if it arrives twice
blocks.applies: the app receives messages from other systems
blocks.check: The same incoming message delivered twice is processed once.

blocks.name: Checkpoints
blocks.what: Save progress in long jobs, so a restart continues instead of starting over
blocks.applies: jobs run for many minutes

blocks.name: Health probes
blocks.what: A simple address that reports whether the app and what it depends on are working
blocks.applies: the app is live and depends on outside services

blocks.name: Heartbeats
blocks.what: Regular still-alive signals from background workers, so a silent failure gets noticed
blocks.applies: background workers run unattended

blocks.name: Race conditions
blocks.what: Bugs where two things happening at once give the wrong result, such as selling the last seat twice
blocks.applies: two requests can change the same thing at once, such as stock, seats or a balance
blocks.check: Two requests at the same moment for the last item: exactly one succeeds. A test fires them together.

blocks.name: Optimistic locking
blocks.what: Detect when two people edited the same record, instead of one silently overwriting the other
blocks.applies: two people can edit the same record

blocks.name: Backups & restore drills
blocks.what: Copy the data regularly, and practise restoring it so you know it works
blocks.applies: the app is going live with data worth keeping

blocks.name: Profiling
blocks.what: Measure where the time actually goes before trying to speed anything up
blocks.applies: something is slow and the cause is unknown

blocks.name: Latency percentiles
blocks.what: Measure how slow the slowest requests are, not just the average
blocks.applies: speed must be measured under real traffic

blocks.name: Load testing
blocks.what: Send heavy fake traffic to find the breaking point before real users do
blocks.applies: a traffic spike is expected

blocks.name: Core Web Vitals
blocks.what: Google's measures of how fast and stable a web page feels to visitors
blocks.applies: public web pages are going live

blocks.name: Slow-query monitoring
blocks.what: Record database queries that take too long, so they can be fixed
blocks.applies: the database is under real use

blocks.name: Caching
blocks.what: Keep the result of costly work so the next request can reuse it
blocks.applies: the same costly work is repeated often

blocks.name: Cache invalidation
blocks.what: Remove or refresh cached data when the real data changes
blocks.applies: the app caches data that changes

blocks.name: Negative caching
blocks.what: Remember that a lookup found nothing, so it is not repeated right away
blocks.applies: lookups that find nothing are repeated often

blocks.name: Dynamic TTL
blocks.what: Let each cached item expire at its own pace, depending on how fast it goes stale
blocks.applies: cached items go stale at different speeds

blocks.name: HTTP caching & ETags
blocks.what: Let browsers reuse a response they already have when it has not changed
blocks.applies: clients fetch the same responses repeatedly

blocks.name: Semantic caching
blocks.what: Reuse an AI answer when a new question means the same as an earlier one
blocks.applies: many users ask an AI model similar questions

blocks.name: Indexing
blocks.what: Add lookup structures to the database so searches do not scan every row
blocks.applies: tables have grown and lookups are slow

blocks.name: N+1 queries
blocks.what: The slowdown when a list runs one database query per item instead of one for all
blocks.applies: lists show related data from the database
blocks.check: Loading a list runs a small, fixed number of queries, not one per item. A test counts them.

blocks.name: Query plans (EXPLAIN)
blocks.what: Ask the database how it will run a query, to see why it is slow
blocks.applies: a specific query is slow

blocks.name: Connection pooling
blocks.what: Reuse a small set of database connections instead of opening a new one per request
blocks.applies: the app is live and opens many database connections

blocks.name: Read replicas
blocks.what: Copies of the database that take the reading load off the main one
blocks.applies: reads overload one database

blocks.name: Materialized views
blocks.what: Store the result of an expensive query and refresh it from time to time
blocks.applies: an expensive report is read often

blocks.name: Bulk operations
blocks.what: Write many rows in one go instead of one at a time
blocks.applies: the app writes many rows at once

blocks.name: Pagination
blocks.what: Load long lists one page at a time
blocks.applies: a list can grow long
blocks.check: Long lists load a page at a time. No request returns every row.

blocks.name: Async I/O
blocks.what: Let one worker handle many waiting requests at once instead of waiting on each in turn
blocks.applies: one worker must handle many waits at once

blocks.name: Bounded fan-out
blocks.what: Run outside calls in parallel, but only a limited number at a time
blocks.applies: the app runs many outside calls in parallel

blocks.name: Debounce & throttle
blocks.what: Wait for a pause, or cap the rate, before acting on rapid repeated triggers such as typing
blocks.applies: the screen fires rapid triggers, such as search while typing
blocks.check: Typing quickly in a live search sends one request after the pause, not one per key.

blocks.name: Pre-aggregation
blocks.what: Keep counts and totals up to date as data changes, instead of adding them up on every request
blocks.applies: counts and totals are slow to compute live

blocks.name: Load leveling
blocks.what: Put bursts of work in a queue and process them at a steady pace
blocks.applies: work arrives in spikes

blocks.name: Load balancing
blocks.what: Spread traffic across several servers
blocks.applies: one server is no longer enough

blocks.name: Autoscaling
blocks.what: Add and remove servers automatically as traffic rises and falls
blocks.applies: traffic rises and falls a lot

blocks.name: Sharding
blocks.what: Split one database's data across several databases
blocks.applies: one database can no longer hold the data

blocks.name: CDN & edge
blocks.what: Serve files from servers close to each user
blocks.applies: users are far from the server

blocks.name: Code splitting
blocks.what: Send the browser only the code the current page needs
blocks.applies: the first page load has become heavy

blocks.name: Image optimization
blocks.what: Serve images at the right size and in the right format, so pages load fast
blocks.applies: a web app with images is going live

blocks.name: Compression
blocks.what: Shrink responses before sending them, so they arrive faster
blocks.applies: a web app is going live

blocks.name: Structured logs
blocks.what: Logs written in one consistent format, with a time, a level and a message, so they can be searched
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: The app logs errors and key events with a time, a level and a message, and never logs a secret or a password.

blocks.name: Error tracking
blocks.what: A service that collects errors from the live app and groups them, so none go unnoticed
blocks.applies: the app is going live

blocks.name: Metrics
blocks.what: Numbers tracked over time, such as requests per minute or errors per hour
blocks.applies: the app is live and its health must be watched

blocks.name: Request IDs
blocks.what: A unique id attached to each request, so its trail can be followed across logs
blocks.applies: a problem must be followed across logs

blocks.name: New-error alerts
blocks.what: A message to you when an error appears that has not been seen before
blocks.applies: the app is live

blocks.name: The four golden signals
blocks.what: Watch traffic, errors, speed and how full the system is; together they show its health
blocks.applies: the app is live and its health must be watched

blocks.name: Per-job metrics
blocks.what: Track how often each background job runs and fails, and how long it takes
blocks.applies: background jobs run under real use

blocks.name: Business metrics
blocks.what: Track the numbers that show whether the app works for people, such as sign-ups and orders
blocks.applies: the app is live

blocks.name: Uptime monitoring
blocks.what: An outside service that checks the app is reachable and tells you when it is not
blocks.applies: the app is going live

blocks.name: Upstream probes
blocks.what: Regular checks that the outside services the app depends on are working
blocks.applies: the app is live and depends on outside services

blocks.name: Actionable alerts
blocks.what: Send an alert only when someone needs to act, and say what to do
blocks.applies: the app is live and sends alerts

blocks.name: On-call and paging
blocks.what: A rota of who responds when the app breaks out of hours
blocks.applies: a team keeps the app running

blocks.name: Runbooks
blocks.what: Written steps for fixing problems that have happened before
blocks.applies: the app is live and things have gone wrong before

blocks.name: Sampled logging
blocks.what: Keep only a share of routine logs once there are too many to store
blocks.applies: logs have become too large

blocks.name: Upstream call log
blocks.what: Record every call to a paid outside service, with what it cost
blocks.applies: the app calls paid outside services

blocks.name: Per-request cost
blocks.what: Work out what each request costs in paid services
blocks.applies: each request costs real money

blocks.name: Cost alerts
blocks.what: Get a warning before a pay-per-use bill passes a limit you set
blocks.applies: the app is going live and uses pay-per-use services

blocks.name: Feature flags
blocks.what: Switch features on or off without releasing new code
blocks.applies: features must be switched without a new release

blocks.name: Staged rollout
blocks.what: Release to a small share of users first, then widen it
blocks.applies: a bad release would hit many users

blocks.name: Kill switch
blocks.what: A way to turn a live feature off at once if it misbehaves
blocks.applies: a live feature may need to be stopped fast

blocks.name: Context window
blocks.what: How much text an AI model can take in at once, counting both the question and the answer
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Token counting
blocks.what: AI models measure text in tokens, which are pieces of words, and charge by them
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Sampling params
blocks.what: Settings such as temperature that make an AI model's answers more varied or more predictable
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Streaming
blocks.what: Show an AI answer as it is being written, instead of after it is finished
blocks.applies: users wait on screen for an AI answer
blocks.check: The AI answer appears on screen as it is generated, and a failure partway shows a clear message.

blocks.name: Prompt caching
blocks.what: Let the AI provider reuse a long prompt you send often, so it costs less
blocks.applies: the app sends the same long prompt often

blocks.name: Tool use
blocks.what: Let an AI model call functions in your code, such as a search, to get facts or take actions
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: JSON mode
blocks.what: A setting that makes an AI model reply in valid JSON
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Structured output
blocks.what: Make the AI reply in a fixed shape that your code checks before using it
blocks.applies: the app's code uses an AI model's answer
blocks.check: AI output used by code is checked against a schema. A malformed answer is retried or refused, never passed on.

blocks.name: Model selection
blocks.what: Pick the AI model that fits the job's cost and quality, and set that choice in one place
blocks.applies: the app calls an AI model
blocks.check: The model name is pinned in one setting, not scattered through the code or left to a moving default.

blocks.name: Non-determinism
blocks.what: The same prompt can give different answers each time, so tests check facts, not wording
blocks.applies: the app calls an AI model
blocks.check: Tests of AI features assert facts that must hold, never the exact wording.

blocks.name: Multimodal input
blocks.what: AI models that take images, audio or files as well as text
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Prompt injection
blocks.what: Stop instructions hidden in content the AI reads from taking control of it
blocks.applies: an AI model reads content its user did not write, or can take actions
blocks.check: Text planted in content the AI reads, telling it to ignore its rules, does not change what the app does or reveal private data.

blocks.name: Jailbreak resistance
blocks.what: Keep the AI within its rules when users try to talk it out of them
blocks.applies: the public can chat with the app's AI

blocks.name: Content moderation
blocks.what: Check what users post, and what the AI writes, for harmful content
blocks.applies: the public can post content or see AI output

blocks.name: PII redaction
blocks.what: Remove personal details from text before it is sent to an AI model
blocks.applies: personal data is sent to an AI model
blocks.check: Personal details the model does not need are removed before the text is sent.

blocks.name: Hallucinations
blocks.what: When an AI model states something false with confidence
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Output guardrails
blocks.what: Check the AI's answer before acting on it or showing it as fact
blocks.applies: AI output triggers actions or is shown as fact
blocks.check: AI output is checked before it is acted on, and an answer outside the allowed bounds is blocked.

blocks.name: Evals
blocks.what: A set of test questions with known good answers, run to measure an AI feature's quality
blocks.applies: an AI feature is central to the app
blocks.check: Each prompt has a small set of example inputs with facts the answer must contain, run as a test.

blocks.name: LLM-as-judge
blocks.what: Use one AI model to grade another's answers at volume
blocks.applies: AI output quality must be graded at volume

blocks.name: A/B testing
blocks.what: Show two versions to different users and measure which works better
blocks.applies: there is enough traffic to compare two versions

blocks.name: LLM tracing
blocks.what: Record each AI call with its input, output, time and cost, to debug and improve it
blocks.applies: AI features run under real use

blocks.name: Budget caps
blocks.what: A spending limit per user and overall that stops AI calls when it is reached
blocks.applies: the app calls a paid AI model
blocks.check: A usage limit per user, and one overall, stops AI calls when reached and shows a clear message.

blocks.name: Batch API
blocks.what: Send large AI jobs to run later at a lower price
blocks.applies: large AI jobs can wait for their results

blocks.name: Model routing
blocks.what: Send each request to the cheapest AI model that can handle it
blocks.applies: AI costs have become significant

blocks.name: Unified interface
blocks.what: One layer in your code that talks to every AI provider the same way
blocks.applies: the app uses more than one AI provider

blocks.name: Embeddings
blocks.what: Numbers that capture what a piece of text means, so similar texts can be found
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Vector database
blocks.what: A database built to find the stored items closest in meaning to a query
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: RAG
blocks.what: The AI first looks up relevant documents, then answers from them
blocks.applies: an AI model answers from the app's own documents
blocks.check: Answers come from the retrieved documents. A question with no matching document gets an honest 'I don't know', not an invented answer.

blocks.name: Chunking
blocks.what: Split documents into small pieces so the right parts can be found and sent to the AI
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Citations
blocks.what: Show which documents an AI answer came from
blocks.applies: an AI model answers from the app's own documents
blocks.check: Each answer shows which documents it used, and each reference opens the right source.

blocks.name: Conversation memory
blocks.what: Let an AI chat remember earlier messages, within the model's limits
blocks.applies: the app has an AI chat
blocks.check: A follow-up question that depends on earlier messages is answered correctly, and a long chat stays within the model's limit.

blocks.name: Knowledge freshness
blocks.what: Keep the documents the AI answers from up to date
blocks.applies: the documents an AI model answers from keep changing

blocks.name: Agent loop
blocks.what: An AI that plans, acts, checks the result, and repeats until the job is done
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: MCP
blocks.what: A standard way to connect AI assistants to tools and data sources
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: Autonomy guardrails
blocks.what: Limits on what an AI agent may do without asking, and how many steps it may take
blocks.applies: an AI model in the app can take actions that change things
blocks.check: Actions that change or delete things need the user's approval, and each run has a cap on its number of steps.

blocks.name: Context engineering
blocks.what: Choose carefully what the AI sees, so it has what it needs and nothing that distracts it
blocks.applies: the term comes up

blocks.name: AI code review
blocks.what: Have an AI review each change for bugs before it is kept
blocks.applies: every app

blocks.name: Verify with AI
blocks.what: Have the AI run and test what it built, instead of trusting that it works
blocks.applies: every app

blocks.name: Live prompts
blocks.what: Change the app's prompts without releasing new code
blocks.applies: prompts need tuning while the app is live

blocks.name: Prompt versioning
blocks.what: Keep a history of prompt changes, so a bad change can be undone
blocks.applies: prompts change while the app is live

blocks.name: Safe templates
blocks.what: Let users edit templates that only fill in blanks and can never run code
blocks.applies: users can edit templates the app fills in

blocks.name: Payments
blocks.what: Take money through a payment provider, so card details never touch your app
blocks.applies: the app takes payments
blocks.check: Card details go straight to the payment provider, and the app never receives or stores a card number. A test-mode payment completes end to end.

blocks.name: Webhook fulfilment
blocks.what: Grant what was bought only when the payment provider confirms the payment
blocks.applies: the app takes payments
blocks.check: Access is granted when the provider's signed webhook arrives, not when the browser returns. A fake webhook is refused, and a repeated one grants once.

blocks.name: Subscriptions
blocks.what: Charge on a schedule, and give or remove access as the subscription changes
blocks.applies: the app sells subscriptions
blocks.check: Subscribing, renewing, cancelling and expiry each change the user's access correctly, driven by the provider's events in test mode.

blocks.name: Failed payments
blocks.what: Handle a renewal that does not go through: tell the user, wait, then remove access
blocks.applies: the app sells subscriptions
blocks.check: A failed renewal marks the account as past due, tells the user, and removes access after the grace period.

blocks.name: Money as cents
blocks.what: Store amounts as whole numbers of the smallest unit, such as cents, to avoid rounding errors
blocks.applies: the app stores or calculates money
blocks.check: Amounts are stored and calculated as whole numbers of the smallest unit, such as cents. A test adds 10 cents and 20 cents and gets exactly 30, and a total over many items has no rounding drift.

blocks.name: File uploads
blocks.what: Let users upload files and get them back later
blocks.applies: users upload files
blocks.check: A valid file uploads and can be opened again. A file that is too large or of the wrong type is refused with a clear message.

blocks.name: Full-text search
blocks.what: Let users find items by the words inside them
blocks.applies: users search the app's content
blocks.check: Search finds items by words in their text, handles no results, and returns only what this user may see.

blocks.name: Realtime updates
blocks.what: Show changes on screen as they happen, without a refresh
blocks.applies: changes must appear without a refresh
blocks.check: A change made in one window appears in another within seconds without a refresh, and the connection recovers after it drops.

blocks.name: Scheduled jobs
blocks.what: Run work at set times, such as a nightly report
blocks.applies: some work runs on a clock
blocks.check: The job runs on schedule, a repeated or overlapping run does no double work, and a failure is logged.

blocks.name: Admin panel
blocks.what: A private area where staff manage the app's data
blocks.applies: the plan names a staff or admin role that manages the app's data
blocks.check: Only admins can open the admin area. A normal user is refused on every admin page and action.

blocks.name: Accessibility
blocks.what: Make the app usable by everyone, including people who use a keyboard or a screen reader
blocks.applies: the app has screens
blocks.check: Every page works by keyboard alone, form fields have labels, and an automated accessibility scan reports no serious problems.

blocks.name: Responsive design
blocks.what: Make every screen work at every size, from phone to desktop
blocks.applies: the app is used on different screen sizes
blocks.check: Every screen is usable at phone width: nothing cut off, no sideways scrolling, buttons large enough to tap.

blocks.name: Screen states
blocks.what: Show something useful while data loads, when there is none, and when loading fails
blocks.applies: the app has screens that load data
blocks.check: Every screen that loads data shows a loading state, an empty state and an error state. Tests force each one.

blocks.name: Localization
blocks.what: Show the app in more than one language, including right-to-left ones where needed
blocks.applies: the app must work in more than one language
blocks.check: All visible text comes from translation files. Switching language changes every screen, including right-to-left layout where the language needs it.

blocks.name: Environments
blocks.what: Separate copies of the app for building, testing and real users, so tests never touch real data
blocks.applies: the app is going live

blocks.name: Store times in UTC
blocks.what: Save every time on one standard clock, and convert it to each user's time zone when showing it
blocks.applies: the app stores dates or times
blocks.check: Times are stored in UTC and shown in the user's time zone. A test saves a time in one time zone and reads it in another, and both show the same moment.

blocks.name: Debugging with AI
blocks.what: Give the AI the exact error and the steps that cause it, and have it find the cause before changing code
blocks.applies: every app

blocks.name: Component library
blocks.what: One shared set of buttons, inputs and dialogs, so every screen looks and behaves the same
blocks.applies: the app has screens

blocks.name: Guessable IDs
blocks.what: Use ids in links that cannot be guessed by counting, such as 1, 2, 3
blocks.applies: ids appear in links or in the API
blocks.check: Ids in links and API responses are not counting numbers. Changing an id by one finds nothing.

blocks.name: Account recovery
blocks.what: A safe way for users who forgot their password to get back in
blocks.applies: users log in with a password
blocks.check: A reset link works once and expires. The reset page gives the same answer whether or not the email has an account.

blocks.name: Soft delete
blocks.what: Hide deleted items instead of erasing them at once, so they can be restored
blocks.applies: the user wants deleted items to be restorable
blocks.check: A deleted item disappears for the user and can be restored for a set period.

blocks.name: Testing
blocks.what: Automated checks that prove each feature works, so a break is caught before users see it
blocks.applies: every app
blocks.check: Every feature has tests for the normal case and at least one failure case, and the check command runs them all.

blocks.name: Playwright
blocks.what: Tests that use the app the way a person does, by clicking through it; Playwright is a common tool for this on the web
blocks.applies: the app has screens
blocks.check: At least one test drives the real app the way a person would, and the check command runs it. Each run starts its own copy of the app and never reuses one that is already running.

blocks.name: CI/CD
blocks.what: Run the checks automatically on every change, and release automatically when they pass
blocks.applies: the app is going live

blocks.name: Domain & DNS
blocks.what: Your app's web address, and the settings that point it at your server
blocks.applies: the app is going live on the internet

blocks.name: noindex
blocks.what: Tell search engines not to list private pages
blocks.applies: a web app with private pages is going live

blocks.name: Social preview
blocks.what: The title, text and image that appear when someone shares a link to your app
blocks.applies: public web pages are going live
